column1: # Shared cases for the branch-list rule. One row is one checkout, one branch,
# and how a branch list under ~/.config/git resolves it.
# Two implementations of that rule exist, one in Go and one in bash, because the
# hook is deployed as a standalone file with no access to the allod binary. This
# table is what keeps them from drifting: tests/git-hooks/protected-refs-policy.sh
# drives the hook with it, and cmd/allod/protection_test.go drives the Go rails.
#   name      case id, also the fixture directory name
#   entries   ';'-separated '<path>=<branch>' lines of the list file, '-' for empty
#   origin    origin remote URL, '-' for a repository with no origin
#   checkout  $HOME-relative path of the MAIN repository
#   worktree  'yes' when the branch under test lives in a linked worktree of it
#   verdict   unprotected, protected (an entry matches the checkout path), or
#             mismatch (an entry matches the origin identity while none matches
#             the path, so the checkout is misplaced)
#   expected  on a mismatch, the entry path the refusal must name; '-' otherwise
# The verdict is the branch-list answer, not what each rail then does with it:
# 'allod change begin' and 'record' refuse a misplaced checkout on every branch,
# while the hook blocks only the entry's branch.
